verdicts.evidence: The early 'untouched' return on an empty list becomes unreachable, but the fall-through gives the same result: [].some(...) is false by definition of the language, so hasFilled=false and the same literal 'untouched' is returned; for any non-empty list the condition was already false. No side effect reordered (reading the template precedes the test in both forms). SENSITIVITY CONTROL: a divergence would require [].some to return true (impossible, ECMAScript semantics) or the two 'untouched' literals to differ (same string). MEASURED on the directory's three regimes: fxc (zero .md — the very path the mutant short-circuits), scaf (template only), ex (filled contracts) — identical states untouched/untouched/filled on both builds; battery byte-identical. Equivalent in the strong sense.

verdicts.evidence: Without trim, the content/template comparison is done on RAW lines: a line that changed only in whitespace counts as 'new'. RECIPE: green example mission; replace runward/decision-matrix.md with the template plus ONE TRAILING SPACE on 3 word-rich lines (fixture fxws — zero new content, 175 words 'added' in the mutant's sense). MEASURED before/after: shipped — '◐ Decision matrix — started, but too close to the template to count as filled', '1 deliverable(s) not filled', EXIT 1; mutated — '✓ Decision matrix', 'Current gate all gates passed', 'All expected deliverables are filled', EXIT 0. DOUBLE SURFACE on the same mission: compliance iso-42001 -> OSCAL runward-gate-verdict 'gaps (exit 1)' -> 'clean (exit 0)' on the 10 components. This is exactly the false green the divergence guard exists to prevent (a whitespace diff passes the gate), and the mutant is one-sided: it can only promote states, never demote them. Nothing sees it, VERIFIED by replaying the 7 legs: all PASS — every fixture of the net diverges through real content (the green ones stay green, the red ones are red for other causes), the smoke.js:451 case (one-byte edit) adds an 'x' line seen identically by both forms; no fixture diverges through whitespace alone.

verdicts.evidence: The early return `if (sections.length === 0) return s` is a SHORTCUT, not a behaviour: when no conformance section is found, `drop` stays empty and `s.split("\n").filter(() => true).join("\n")` rebuilds exactly `s`. Measured 2026-09-13 on three fixtures built from templates/mission/execution-topology.md (the template has 1 placeholder, so the placeholders floor does not short-circuit the divergence guard, which is the code measured): bare template -> untouched / untouched; template WITHOUT a conformance section -> added=0 words=0 -> in-progress, identical on the shipped build and the mutated build; section moved to the end of the note with two lines written -> added=2 words=36 -> in-progress, identical. None of the three figures moves, including that of the fixture that reaches the mutated branch. SENSITIVITY CONTROL, in the same pass: the second survivor named by the same ratchet (`i < end` -> `i <= end`, the loop that eats one line too many) flips this last fixture from in-progress to FILLED — added=3 words=38 — because it removes on the TEMPLATE side the `## Cross-references` heading that ends the section, so that the copy of that heading in the content becomes the "operator's divergence". So the instrument does tell a mutant that changes a verdict from a mutant that changes none, on this same file and these same fixtures: the equivalence of this one is measured, not deduced from an absence of observation.
